title: How to Track TikTok Competitors Without Following Them
summary: See what competitors run on TikTok without following them: Creative Center, the EU Commercial Content Library, profile browsing and free ad library pages.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- You do not need to follow a competitor to see their TikTok ads. Four routes work without it: TikTok's Creative Center, TikTok's Commercial Content Library, a logged-out look at their profile, and third-party ad libraries.
- **Creative Center** shows top-performing ads by region, industry and objective. It will not show every ad from one named brand.
- **The Commercial Content Library** is TikTok's official ad archive for ads shown in the EU and neighbouring markets. You can search by advertiser.
- Outside those markets, the best view of one brand's TikTok ads is an ad library that tracks them, such as[the Sprites TikTok ads library](https://www.sprites.ai/tiktok-ads-library) .
- Following is not what exposes you. Account activity is invisible to the brand unless you like, comment or follow.


TikTok is where many brands now test creative first, which makes it a good place to watch competitors. The catch is that TikTok has no single "ad library" like Meta's that covers every ad worldwide. You assemble the picture from several sources. This guide shows which source answers which question.


## Does following a competitor matter?


Following is not required to view anything public, and it does two things you may not want. It can tell the brand a new account noticed them, and it changes your For You feed so that you see more of their content and less of the rest of your market. For research, a clean approach is a separate account or a logged-out browser.


Watching, searching and scrolling do not notify anyone. Likes, comments, shares and follows do.


## Route 1: TikTok Creative Center


The Creative Center is TikTok's own research site for advertisers. It is free and does not need you to run ads. For competitor tracking, the useful parts are:


- **Top Ads.** A gallery of high-performing ads that you can filter by region, industry, objective, ad format and time window. Each ad shows engagement signals so you can see what is working in a category.
- **Trends.** Rising hashtags, sounds, creators and videos, by region.
- **Keyword insights.** What phrases show up in top ad text.


What it will not do is list every ad from the brand you name. It is a curated view of what performs, not an archive. Use it to learn what competitors in your industry are doing, then use another route for a specific brand. A full tour is in the[TikTok Creative Center guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/tiktok-creative-center-guide) .


## Route 2: The Commercial Content Library


Under the EU's Digital Services Act, TikTok has to publish an archive of ads shown to users in the EU. That archive is the Commercial Content Library. It is the closest thing TikTok has to Meta's Ad Library.


- You can search by advertiser name or keyword and filter by the country where the ad ran and by date.
- For ads shown in the EU, entries include details such as when the ad ran, the advertiser, and information on targeting and reach.
- It covers the countries where the rules apply. A US-only campaign will not appear.


It is the best official source for a brand that advertises in Europe, and for any large brand that runs the same creative in several countries, since the creative often appears in Europe as well. Coverage and filters change, so check TikTok's Help Center for the current scope.


## Route 3: Watch their profile, logged out


A competitor's TikTok profile shows organic posts and, often, posts they promote through Spark Ads. A promoted organic post looks like any other post to the viewer, so the profile alone will not tell you which are paid.


1. Open the profile in a private browser window. TikTok's web version lets you view public profiles.
2. Sort by Popular. Videos with outsized views relative to the account are often the ones being paid to reach more people.
3. Read the comments. Questions like "where do I buy this?" tell you the ad is working.
4. Check the profile link. A product page or a landing page is a campaign destination.


To read how Spark Ads turn posts into ads, see[TikTok Spark Ads](https://www.sprites.ai/tiktok-spark-ads) .


## Route 4: Ad libraries that track TikTok


For brands outside the EU, third-party libraries fill the gap. The[Sprites TikTok ads library](https://www.sprites.ai/tiktok-ads-library) collects TikTok ads in one place and is free to read. Brand pages live at` /{brand}-ads` , for instance[Gymshark ads](https://www.sprites.ai/gymshark-ads) and[Duolingo ads](https://www.sprites.ai/duolingo-ads) , and category pages cover whole markets, such as[fashion ads](https://www.sprites.ai/fashion-ads) and[fitness ads](https://www.sprites.ai/fitness-ads) .


The advantage is that you can compare several brands without an account, and move from TikTok to the same brands' Meta ads on one site. If you also watch Facebook and Instagram, see[how to see competitors' Facebook ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/how-to-see-competitors-facebook-ads) .


## Which route to use


Question Best route


What works in my industry right now? Creative Center, Top Ads


What sounds and hashtags are rising? Creative Center, Trends


What is brand X running in Europe? Commercial Content Library


What is brand X running outside Europe? An ad library that tracks TikTok


Which of their posts get promoted? Profile, sorted by popular, with comments read


## A 30-minute weekly routine


1. **Ten minutes in Top Ads.** Filter to your industry and objective, and save three ads that stop you. Write why in one line each.
2. **Ten minutes on three competitors.** Open each in the library route that fits, and note new ads since last week.
3. **Ten minutes on structure.** For each saved ad, log the first two seconds (the hook), the format (talking head, demo, UGC, slideshow), the sound and the call to action.


After a month, patterns show up: which hooks competitors reuse, how long videos run, how often they refresh. The method for pulling hooks apart is in[how to analyze competitor ads for winning hooks](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/analyze-competitor-ads-winning-hooks) , and the cost side is in[TikTok ads cost](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/tiktok-ads-cost) .


## What none of these show


No route shows TikTok ad spend, conversions or click-through rate for a competitor. TikTok publishes none of it. What you can infer is how long a creative runs, how often a brand refreshes, and what the audience says in the comments. An ad that has been live for weeks is probably paying for itself.

## Frequently asked questions


### Can I see a competitor's TikTok ads without following them?


Yes. Public ads and profiles can be viewed without following. Use TikTok's Creative Center for top ads in your industry, the Commercial Content Library for ads shown in the EU, and a third-party ad library for the rest.


### Does TikTok tell a brand who viewed its videos?


No. Viewing does not notify the brand. It appears only as an aggregate view count. Likes, comments, shares and follows are visible to the account.


### Is there a TikTok version of the Facebook Ad Library?


Partly. The Commercial Content Library is TikTok's official archive, but it covers ads shown in the EU and neighbouring markets, not the whole world. Third-party libraries cover other regions.


### How do I tell which TikTok posts are ads?


Paid ads show a Sponsored label in the feed. Spark Ads, which promote a creator's or brand's organic post, carry the same label in the feed but look like ordinary posts on the profile.


### Can I see how much a competitor spends on TikTok ads?


No. TikTok does not publish spend for commercial ads. Run length and how often a creative is refreshed are the best signals of what is working.


### Do I need a TikTok Ads account to use Creative Center?


No. Creative Center can be browsed without running ads, though some features ask you to sign in.
